title: The 23 new wave-0 platform stories have no release date
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1.xlsx
description: RWB-PLT-N001 to RWB-PLT-N012 (16 stories with their CON variants) and RWB-PLT-NF01 to RWB-PLT-NF08 (8 stories) carry an empty Release in the Service Story Catalog v1, while the 48 platform stories that come from a v6 legacy key carry 30 November 2026 or 31 December 2026 (tentative). The v6 Build Sequence has no platform block, so it does not supply a date either.
evidence: Service Story Catalog v1, sheet Stories: Release is empty for the 23 rows whose Story starts RWB-PLT-N; v6 Sequence has 115 items and none of them is RWB-PLT-N001 to RWB-PLT-N012.
proposed: Assign the wave-0 platform stories to the Window 1 release (E1, 30 November 2026, tentative) or name their own wave-0 release date.

title: No review window covers the wave-0 platform block
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Build Sequence Epic 1 and Epic 2 v6.xlsx
description: v6 opens at Window 1 (2 Nov to 13 Nov) with Epic 1 items. The realignment puts 65 platform stories (wave 0) in front of Window 1 (Template and Rules §R5.6), but neither v6 nor the story catalog gives that block a review window or a set of dates.
evidence: v6 By window: Window 1 starts 2 Nov; v6 Sequence item 1 is RWB-E1-044 in Window 1; 65 RWB-PLT stories exist in the catalog with wave 0 and no window.
proposed: Add a wave-0 window before 2 November, or fold the 65 platform stories into Window 1 and extend it.

title: Window dates end in January 2027 while the new stories release through June 2027
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1.xlsx
description: The v6 windows run 2 November 2026 to 22 January 2027 (Window 1 to Epic 3). The service stories that the same 115 items split into carry release dates up to 30 June 2027 (tentative), so a story pulled in Window 2 may have a release after the last window of the sheet.
evidence: v6 By window: 28 Dec to 22 Jan is the last window. Service Story Catalog v1: Release values include 30 June 2027 (tentative) and 28 February 2027 (tentative).
proposed: Keep the two-week windows as review points and let the per-story release date stand, or re-cut the windows to the release plan.

title: Two retired items still carry v6 windows and dependencies
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Build Sequence Epic 1 and Epic 2 v6.xlsx
description: RWB-E1-014 (decision log copy to the data lake) and RWB-TE-007 (scheduled jobs on Quartz) are retired under §R6 and have no new story, yet v6 still lists them with a window, dates and dependants, and two other items (RWB-E1-056, RWB-E1-017) still name them in Depends on.
evidence: v6 Sequence items 19 and 21; Template and Rules §R6 Retired.
proposed: Drop the two rows when the tracker is cut over, or keep them struck through with 'retired, not pulled' as this version does.

title: The v6 module column cannot show who builds a split row
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Build Sequence Epic 1 and Epic 2 v6.xlsx
description: A v6 row carries one monolith module (P1 to P10), one owner and one window. After the split, one v6 item is up to nine stories in up to six services, so neither the module column nor the By module counts can show the service or the lane that builds part of the item.
evidence: v6 Sequence: 115 rows, 15 distinct module values, one row per item. Catalog: 530 stories carry the 115 legacy keys, across 19 services plus the platform and integration epics.
proposed: Keep the module column for traceability and report load by service and lane, as the new sheet 'By service and lane' does.
